refutation.reason: No panel refutation was recorded for this finding — it reached the workup undisputed. The opposing/confirmatory position is the executed probe in SS3 of the packet: Serving-name probe (`probes/closingA_serving_name.py`) runs `core.run_verification` with a primary seat that raises and a fallback seat (`fbseat`) that serves the job and raises a NEW finding. At HEAD the code binds `serving_name, serving_fn = name, providers[name]` (core.py:3847), reassigns `serving_name, serving_fn = fb_name, fb_fn` when the fallback serves (core.py:3894), and normalizes new findings with `serving_name` (core.py:3920). Probe output: - reviewer report: `provider='fbseat' fallback_for='primary' status='ok'` - new finding: `sources=['fbseat']` — attributed to the seat that actually produced it Attribution by `serving_name` is fidelity-correct: it names the provider actually called, and it is consistent with the reviewer report (`provider`/`fallback_for`) and the seat metadata taken from the same variable. Substituting `name` would credit the failed primary — a seat that never ran — recreating the record-fidelity defect class the owner had fixed under `78ddf4d5ea27` (a record must never name a model/seat that was not the one actually serving). Re-run at HEAD `61e137d` produced byte-identical output (sha256 unchanged, §5).
